question: Should `socket.drain` preserve the existing Gateway slow-subscriber drop behavior, or become an explicit fail-closed teardown signal that may close slow WebSocket clients?
rationale: The PR's usefulness depends on a Gateway event/backpressure contract that affects message delivery and client availability; code review can recommend the safer default, but maintainers need to own any intentional fail-closed public behavior.

options.title: Preserve existing overload semantics
options.body: Use the existing `dropIfSlow: true` behavior for drain events, share the subscription-key resolver, and document/normalize the new event before merge.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed drains
options.body: Allow slow clients to be closed on teardown only with explicit protocol docs, tests, and upgrade proof that this is the intended contract.

options.title: Pause the public event
options.body: Keep the PR open or narrow it until maintainers decide whether a new public Gateway event is the right API surface.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing overload semantics
recommendation.body: Use the existing `dropIfSlow: true` behavior for drain events, share the subscription-key resolver, and document/normalize the new event before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent history point to Peter as the strongest Gateway/protocol routing owner for this contract choice.
